items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my youngest, Wayne, who now actually is owner of the Jazz Showcase... Yeah, actually Wayne took over all the problems of that... Wayne and I were driving around... Wayne and his buddy Chuck got ahold of it

ctx.x: The CHA, yes it was row houses, and it was fine and it was mixed. White and black. And my wife was black. I married her, and we had five kids, including my youngest, Wayne, who now actually is owner of the Jazz Showcase, and he’s the one who built this room in fact. Nothing bad happened there until they built the high-rises, and then the gangs came in. That’s when shit hit the fan.

I just think - going back once again - that Roosevelt University, and of course... was it Edward Sparling.... The curriculum as it was stated was based upon social justice, and so it seems to me there was a - he was a real pioneer of challenging the time.
